'''Taupota''' is an [[Oceanic language]] of the [[Milne Bay Province]], [[Papua New Guinea]]. It appears to be a [[dialect chain]], with southern varieties called Wa'ema and western Wedau.

The Wedau variety, which varies between villages, was adopted by Anglican missionaries who settled in [[Dogura, Papua New Guinea|Dogura]] and so became the ''[[lingua franca]]'' for the southern coast of [[Goodenough Bay]].<ref name="Kahn1993">{{cite book |author=Miriam Kahn |date=30 December 1993 |title=Always Hungry, Never Greedy: Food and the Expression of Gender in a Melanesian Society |publisher=Waveland Press |isbn=1478609184 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4ZgYAAAAQBAJ |pages=16–18}}</ref>
